A few gentle starting points for a page that feels hard to begin.

A blank page can feel like an invitation. On another day, it can feel like another thing asking something of you.

You do not need to make a record of everything. You might begin with a colour, the weather outside, or one word that feels close enough.

Try a smaller beginning

  • Today feels…
  • Something I wish I could say is…
  • For the next hour, I would like…

You can stop there. A sentence does not need to become a story. A page does not need to be finished to have held something for you.
Offering something thoughtful while leaving room for the person receiving it.

When someone you love is going through cancer, choosing a gift can feel surprisingly difficult. You may want to show care without asking them to reassure you or feel a particular way.

Keep the message simple

A note such as “Thinking of you. There is no need to reply” can leave space for whatever kind of day they are having.

Let the gift belong to them

If you give a journal, there is no need to ask to read it or check whether they have started. They may use it now, later, occasionally or in a way you did not expect.

You can offer practical help too: a specific errand, a meal or a lift, with an easy way to say no.
There is no right way to use a journal
Skip a page. Write one word. Start again when you want to.

You do not owe your journal a daily entry. It is there when you want somewhere to put a thought, make a mark or pause for a moment.

Make it fit the day

On a busy day, one word might be enough. On a quieter day, you might want more room. You can begin in the middle, return to an old prompt or leave something unfinished.

Privacy is your choice

You can share a page if you want to. You can also keep every word to yourself. Writing something down does not create an obligation to explain it.

The useful rhythm is the one that suits you.
